title: An object cut off inside its section header table
request: cut.o: the first 360 bytes of a 776-byte object. The ELF header is intact and says e_shoff 328, e_shnum 7, e_shentsize 64 — a table that would end at 776
response: The linker exits non-zero with a message naming `cut.o`, and writes no output file. 328 + 7 * 64 is past the end of a 360-byte file, and that is the whole check
note: Compute the end of every table in a width that cannot overflow and compare it with the length of the buffer you read. `e_shnum * 64` in 32 bits is enough to wrap for e_shnum near 65535.

title: An empty input file
response: A non-zero exit naming the file is the clearest answer. GNU ld instead reads it as an empty linker script and exits 0 — with an output that has no PT_LOAD, no entry point and cannot be executed, which is what the suite checks
note: Whatever you decide, decide it: the one outcome that is always wrong is exit 0 next to a file the shell will happily try to run.
